analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 999-1461), which are historical release notes for v0.9.18 through v0.9.22. The patch excerpt shows the actual change is a new v0.10.2 candidate section at head lines 11-246, which is outside the supplied text units. This is a documentation-only change, so no executable security behavior changed in the visible evidence. I read the historical entries for statements that would invalidate the canonical threat model, and found none. The entries reaffirm existing controls: encrypted SSD prefix cache with a write budget, external cache volume UUID pinning and encryption, provider endpoint-resumption custody limited to protocol 1, logout revocation, App Attest dispatch responsiveness, and official-build registration. They match T-041 (cache storage, SEC-035 accepted risk) and the TB-011 / T-053 / T-054 coverage. They do not loosen the 30-minute TTL or the account isolation.

The patch excerpt for the new v0.10.2 notes is truncated and its full text was not supplied. It mentions 4-bit balanced SSD checkpoints for Nemotron 3.5 Super and GLM-5.3-Flash under new cache namespaces, logprobs gating that depends on the platform and fleet converging, and cache-routing allowlist tuple prerequisites. Those describe code changes whose source was not supplied. Whether the new checkpoint encoding preserves the T-041 mitigations (HMAC lookup tags, AAD binding, salt scoping, layout/profile identity rejection) must be verified against the provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD source changes in other batches. Another open point is whether the logprobs exposure interacts with the cache timing oracle. No finding is raised from changelog text alone.
